title: Speech models in Ollama
summary: Ollama now supports speech models, starting with Phonon from Gradium. Read text aloud in five languages and dozens of voices, streamed as it is generated, over 100 times faster than real time on Apple Silicon.
body_markdown:
Ollama can now turn text into speech. The first speech model is[Phonon](https://ollama.com/library/phonon) , a family of small, state-of-the-art text-to-speech models from[Gradium](https://gradium.ai/) . Speech models are now available for macOS, with Windows and Linux support coming soon.


```text
ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama."


```


```text


```


Unedited output from Ollama 0.40.11 on a MacBook Pro with M5 Max.


## Performance on Apple Silicon


On Apple Silicon, Ollama is accelerated by MLX, Apple’s machine learning framework, for state-of-the-art throughput. On a MacBook Pro with M5 Max, Ollama was 35% faster than the next fastest engine, Gradium’s own runtime.


Throughput


Times faster than real time


Measured on a MacBook Pro with M5 Max, generating 45 seconds of speech. Median of 10 runs. Gradium's own runtime, ptts, uses 8-bit weights on the CPU, fp16 on the Neural Engine and f32 on the GPU; Ollama runs the model in bf16.


Ollama’s implementation is just as accurate, matching the word error rate of the reference implementation in Hugging Face Transformers:


Accuracy


Word error rate


Lower is better. 200 sentences from the Seed-TTS English test set, transcribed with Whisper large-v3.


## Voices


Choose a voice with` --voice` , or` voice` in the API:


```text
ollama run phonon --voice Hadley "Hello from Ollama."


```


The voices come from Gradium’s[voice catalog](https://huggingface.co/gradium/phonon-voices) .` ollama show phonon` lists them all.


## Languages


Model Language


` phonon` English


` phonon:40m-fr` French


` phonon:40m-de` German


` phonon:40m-es` Spanish


` phonon:40m-pt` Portuguese


` phonon:40m-multilingual` All five


` phonon` is released under Apache 2.0. The 40M models are released under CC BY-NC 4.0, which limits them to noncommercial use.


## Read replies aloud


Pipe a chat model’s reply into Phonon. Text is spoken as it arrives, so the reply starts playing after its first sentence:


```text
ollama run gemma4 --hidethinking "Tell me a fun fact about owls in two sentences." | ollama run phonon


```


Run` ollama run phonon` with no text to type lines at a prompt, or redirect the output to save a WAV file:


```text
ollama run phonon "Save this to a file." > speech.wav


```


## API


Phonon works with the OpenAI-compatible` /v1/audio/speech` endpoint, so existing code that uses the OpenAI SDK only needs a new base URL.


```text
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/audio/speech \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
"model": "phonon",
"voice": "Zoey",
"input": "Hello from Ollama."
}' --output speech.wav
```


```text
from openai import OpenAI


client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1", api_key="ollama")


with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(
model="phonon",
voice="Zoey",
input="Hello from Ollama.",
response_format="wav",
) as response:
response.stream_to_file("speech.wav")
```


```text
import fs from "node:fs"
import OpenAI from "openai"


const openai = new OpenAI({ baseURL: "http://localhost:11434/v1", apiKey: "ollama" })


const response = await openai.audio.speech.create({
model: "phonon",
voice: "Zoey",
input: "Hello from Ollama.",
response_format: "wav",
})
fs.writeFileSync("speech.wav", Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()))
```


The response streams while the audio is generated, so it can play right away:


```text
curl -sN http://localhost:11434/v1/audio/speech \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"model": "phonon", "input": "Playback starts right away."}' \
| ffplay -nodisp -autoexit -loglevel error -


```


Audio is 24 kHz mono, returned as WAV by default or as raw 16-bit samples with` "response_format": "pcm"` .


## Get started


Speech models run on Apple Silicon Macs.[Download Ollama](https://ollama.com/download) 0.40.11 or later, then pull Phonon:


```text
ollama pull phonon


```


For more information, see:


- [Phonon model page](https://ollama.com/library/phonon)
- [Speech documentation](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech)
- [OpenAI compatibility](https://docs.ollama.com/api/openai-compatibility)
- [Gradium’s voice catalog](https://huggingface.co/gradium/phonon-voices)
